subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should the macOS Dashboard browser Control UI ever receive native device or operator tokens, or must browser injection be limited to configured shared token/password/auth flow across open, fast-path, and endpoint-reload paths?
rationale: The linked issue and docs support a shared-secret browser boundary, but the sibling parity issue and PR expect native/operator token reuse; either direction changes credential handling and upgrade behavior, so a maintainer must choose the boundary before merge.

options.title: Adopt shared-token-only browser injection
options.body: Rebase this PR, update all Dashboard browser-auth paths including endpoint reloads, and close the conflicting native-token parity direction after proof passes.

options.title: Adopt native-token parity
options.body: Close or rewrite this PR and continue with the sibling parity approach so Dashboard browser auth can use the same resolved native/operator token as native clients.

options.title: Pause for documented auth design
options.body: Keep both drafts paused until a maintainer documents the Dashboard browser auth policy and expected upgrade behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared-token-only browser injection
recommendation.body: Rebase this PR, update all Dashboard browser-auth paths including endpoint reloads, and close the conflicting native-token parity direction after proof passes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced and recently maintained the central Dashboard window and endpoint-reload code paths involved in this auth boundary.
